record.context_brief: computing affine normals in high dimension
record.original_question: How can one numerically calculate the affine normal of a hypersurface M^n ⊂ ℝ^n when the dimension n is large?

evidence.quote: Question 2.4. How does one numerically calculate affine normal for a hypersurface M^n⊂ ℝ^n when n is large ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M^n \subset \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ be a smooth, locally strictly convex hypersurface (so that its second fundamental form is definite and the Blaschke/equiaffine structure is well defined). At each point $p \in M$, the affine (Blaschke) normal vector $\xi(p)$ is the transverse vector field uniquely characterized by the conditions that (i) it induces the equiaffine volume form coinciding with the volume form of the affine metric (Berwald–Blaschke metric) $h$ obtained from the second fundamental form normalized by $|\det II|^{1/(n+2)}$, and (ii) the induced volume form is parallel with respect to the induced connection. Equivalently, if $M$ is locally given as a graph $x_{n+1} = f(x_1,\dots,x_n)$ with $\det(\partial^2 f) \ne 0$, the affine normal can be expressed in terms of $f$ and its first and second derivatives via classical formulas involving $|\det(\partial^2 f)|^{-1/(n+2)}$ and the inverse Hessian.

Devise an efficient numerical algorithm that, given access to a point $p \in M$ and to local first- and second-order data of $M$ near $p$ (for example, samples of a defining function or of a graph parametrization), computes an accurate approximation of the affine normal vector $\xi(p)$, with computational cost and numerical stability that remain practical when the ambient dimension $n+1$ is large. Analyze the conditioning, complexity, and error of such an algorithm.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a specific algorithm or paper addressing efficient numerical computation of the Blaschke affine normal for hypersurfaces in high ambient dimension. Standard references describe the analytic definition of the affine normal and there is work on affine-normal geometric flows, but no clear resolution of the high-dimensional numerical computation question was found. Status is therefore unclear from the available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Contraction of convex hypersurfaces by their affine normal
status_evidence.snippet: Theoretical work on flows by the affine normal of convex hypersurfaces.
status_evidence.claim: The affine normal is a classical object studied analytically; this reference focuses on geometric flow rather than numerical computation in high dimension.

status_evidence.title: Affine maximal hypersurfaces (Xu-Jia Wang, ICM 2002)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of affine maximal hypersurfaces and the equiaffine structure.
status_evidence.claim: Discusses theory of affine normals but does not provide a numerical algorithm for high-dimensional computation.
